item.title: Fed Governor Cook speech 'The U.S. Economy in Global Context' (Central Bank of Chile annual conference, Santiago; Fed posted 17:15 GMT Fri Nov 20 = 01:15 Taipei Sat Nov 21). On policy: she supported September's hike to 3.75-4.00%, DISSENTED in October preferring another +25bp; 'In a different environment, the Committee could afford to be patient, but ... we do not have that luxury'; 'skeptical that September's single 1/4 point rate increase will be enough'; inflation data since September (incl. last week's reports) 'fail to provide me with sufficient evidence' inflation is returning to a sustainable path; 'waiting longer ... risks getting behind the curve. If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later'; number and magnitude of future adjustments to be informed by the economy's reaction. Outlook: growth 'strong - and accelerating' (Q3 GDP 3.4% annualized), est. Oct PCE 3.8% y/y / core 3.2%, inflation above 2% for 67 months, unemployment 4.1%, Oct payrolls +165k, claims 4-wk avg ~195k; financial conditions 'too accommodative', AI buildout not curtailed. She did NOT state a specific December move or size (Yahoo Finance: 'stopped short'); Reuters: markets broadly expect a December 8-9 hike. Interpretation (not her words): hawkish, consistent with at least +25bp in December; explicit 50bp call = UNKNOWN/none
